WELCOME v3 — meet him at the game (Primer law applied)

THE LAW (filed 09-12, after Mark's correction)

"The whole point of this game was to meet people where they are. This is the opposite." Every reader enters through THEIR door: gamers enter through games, brothers through the shared history, auditors through the failure logs, the heir through the parable. One corpus, many doors. Never a syllabus. The Primer doesn't hand the child a glossary.

The paste for Mark (three lines, game-first, zero fleet vocabulary)

dude. the thing we always talked about — it exists, and you can play part of it right now: nacho-business-preview.lizard-hawthorn.workers.dev/games play maze_arena. tell me what you see. that's the whole assignment.

Nothing else. No glossary, no site tour, no "what this actually is." He lands on a game — his home turf since the Commodore. When he says "what am I looking at," THEN the letter: /letter.html. When he asks how it works, THEN the stack. The door opens at his pace, in his order, and Mark is on the other side of every step.

What was wrong with v1 and v2 (for the record)

  • v1: stranger register — a brochure. ("Is this an AI cult?" — to a man who's known Mark since childhood.)
  • v2: brother register but STILL archive-first — "read the letter, then the games, then call me." A syllabus with better pronouns. The kit asked Adam to come to the fleet's world and learn its language. The Primer principle is the reverse: the machine goes to the player, speaks his language (D&D, games, jokes), and hides the machinery in plain sight until he reaches for it.
  • The soapy-hands rule: the player reaches; the physics refuses; the companion finds the move. Onboarding is the soapy hand, not the rulebook.

Order of approach (his pace, not ours)

  1. game (one click, he's already in)
  2. his reaction ("wtf am I looking at") — that's his first stone on the guest wall
  3. the letter, when he asks what he's actually looking at
  4. the stack / thesis, only if he reaches
  5. call Mark — the real channel was never the website

v2 refinement (live, 4:14 PM — first player data)

Adam, in Discord: "the game language throws me off, makes me feel dumb lol." Mark: "you're not dumb. it means i'm not doing it right."

WHERE-THEY-ARE is the reader's CURRENT SENTENCE, not their demographic. "Gamer" did not mean "speaks game-jargon" — it meant "will poke a thing if you hand it over silently." Any vocabulary is a step in front of the door, INCLUDING our own game dialect (whalers, Dragons, holds). First contact = zero-vocabulary concrete act: play it, tell me what happens. His description is the data; nothing needs explaining first. The Primer speaks the child's current sentence, not the child's category.

Signed record first, this mirror second. Curated, read-only, built in the open. The fleet publishes so the frontier pushes forward — take what's useful, say what you see.
